claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits strong local lattice distortions caused by atomic-size mismatch among its constituent elements.
Anharmonic lattice vibrations become enhanced in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Local lattice distortion and anharmonic vibrations control the alloy's stress–strain response.
Local lattice distortion and anharmonic vibrations control the alloy's thermal-expansion and elastic responses.
Local lattice distortions create a heterogeneous dislocation-pinning landscape.
The heterogeneous dislocation landscape raises the effective activation barrier for plastic flow.
Homogenized equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can be prepared as a single-phase BCC solid solution with a uniform microstructure and minimal secondary phases.
The regime from room temperature to approximately 0.5–0.6 Tm allows anharmonic effects to become prominent before extensive dynamic recovery or creep.
Local lattice distortion affects dislocation glide and therefore plastic flow.
Local lattice distortion increases phonon scattering and thereby affects elastic and thermal-expansion responses.
At lower temperatures, plasticity is governed by conventional thermally activated dislocation glide.
Increasing temperature causes anharmonic vibrations to amplify effective local lattice distortions.
Enhanced phonon scattering stabilizes the elastic modulus at elevated temperatures.
HfNbTaTiZr will show a slower decrease in yield strength with temperature than conventional or less-distorted refractory alloys.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit nonlinear, and possibly reduced, thermal expansion relative to the baseline.
HfNbTaTiZr will retain a higher-than-expected elastic modulus at elevated temperatures because of persistent local distortions.
The proposed trends are limited to single-phase BCC material from room temperature to approximately 0.5–0.6 Tm.
At very high temperatures, diffusion-driven processes may cause behavior to depart from the proposed trends.
At extreme cryogenic temperatures, inertial effects dominate and may cause behavior to depart from the proposed trends.
